courseTitle: The Ancient Maya — Rainforest Cities & Maths (c. 2000 BC–AD 1500)
disclaimer: The History Revision Hub — Key Stage 2 Primary History Mind Map.

root.label: The Ancient Maya
root.gloss: How Maya communities built limestone rainforest cities, carved 800 glyphs, invented place-value zero, traded cacao, and still thrive over seven million strong today.

children.label: 1. Rainforest Cities & Kings
children.gloss: Across Mesoamerica’s three zones, Maya engineers stored water in cenotes and grew Three Sisters crops to feed 40+ stone city-states ruled by holy Ajaw kings and queens.

children.label: 1. Stone Cities in Rainforests
children.q2Chain: Three Mesoamerican zones trade jade & obsidian → Cenotes, reservoirs & Three Sisters crops → Stone pyramids contrast Saxon timber huts
children.gloss: Three Mesoamerican zones trade jade & obsidian → Cenotes, reservoirs & Three Sisters crops → Stone pyramids contrast Saxon timber huts

children.label: Mesoamerica’s Three Zones
children.gloss: Maya families settled volcanic highlands, rainforest lowlands, and limestone Yucatán, building stone cities without metal ploughs or wheels.

children.label: Highland Jade, Obsidian & Quetzals
children.gloss: Volcanic black obsidian, green jade; Cloud-forest emerald quetzal feathers.

children.label: Rainforest Lowlands & Flat Yucatán
children.gloss: Jaguars prowled tall rainforest trees; Built without wheels or metal.

children.label: → Porous Rock Needed Clever Water
children.gloss: Rain sank through porous limestone; Pushed towns to store rainwater.

children.label: Cenotes & Three Sisters Crops
children.gloss: Engineers tapped Yucatán cenotes and plastered Tikal reservoirs while farmers grew maize, climbing beans, and wide squash together.

children.label: Sinkhole Cenotes & Chultun Tanks
children.gloss: Plastered giant stone Tikal reservoirs; Carved stepped hillside farm terraces.

children.label: Maize, Climbing Beans & Squash
children.gloss: Maize poles held soil-rich beans; Wide squash leaves blocked weeds.

children.label: → Fed Tens of Thousands
children.gloss: Raised wetland fields grew surpluses; Supported masons and plaza markets.

children.label: Stone Plazas vs Saxon Britain
children.gloss: Around AD 900, Uxmal and Tikal gleamed with painted limestone step-pyramids whereas Anglo-Saxon Britain farmed around small wooden halls.

children.label: Step-Pyramids at Tikal & Uxmal
children.gloss: Built whitewashed courtyard stone homes; Traded cacao, cotton, salt, honey.

children.label: Saxon Britain Used Timber Halls
children.gloss: Small wooden villages across Atlantic; Used iron ploughs, zero pyramids.

children.label: Proved Stone Cities Needed Zero Iron
children.gloss: Painted stone plazas and observatories; Thrived through clever farming teamwork.

children.label: 2. Pyramids, Pakal & Queens
children.q2Chain: 40+ rival city-states under holy Ajaw lords → King Pakal’s 68-year reign & jade mask → Royal Maya women & Bonampak murals
children.gloss: 40+ rival city-states under holy Ajaw lords → King Pakal’s 68-year reign & jade mask → Royal Maya women & Bonampak murals

children.label: 40+ City-States & Holy Ajaws
children.gloss: Like Ancient Greece, over forty independent Maya city-states competed under sacred K’uhul Ajaw rulers atop corbel-vaulted pyramids.

children.label: Rival Tikal, Calakmul & Palenque
children.gloss: Never formed one single empire; Copán and Yaxchilán forged alliances.

children.label: Holy Ajaw Lords Atop Pyramids
children.gloss: Spoke with gods for rain; Crowned pyramids with corbelled vaults.

children.label: → Rulers Built Grand Jade Tombs
children.gloss: Stood high above red plazas; Showed divine favour in stone.

children.label: King Pakal & Jade Tomb Mask
children.gloss: Crowned aged twelve in AD 615, King Pakal ruled Palenque for 68 years and lay buried wearing a life-sized green jade mosaic mask.

children.label: Crowned Aged 12; Ruled 68 Years
children.gloss: Wore jade collars, quetzal feathers; Built four-storey stone watchtower.

children.label: Hidden Stairway & Green Jade Mask
children.gloss: Buried beneath Temple of Inscriptions; Life-sized green jade mosaic mask.

children.label: → Guided by Strong Royal Women
children.gloss: Mother guided young Pakal first; Royal queens shaped alliances next.

children.label: Warrior Queens & Palace Murals
children.gloss: Lady Sak K’uk’ and warrior queen Lady Six Sky appeared on stone stelae while Bonampak’s murals captured royal music and jaguar pelts.

children.label: Lady Sak K’uk’ & Lady Six Sky
children.gloss: Sak K’uk’ crowned young Pakal; Six Sky rebuilt Naranjo AD 682.

children.label: Bonampak Murals & Turtle Drums
children.gloss: Blew horns; beat turtle shells; Danced in spotted jaguar pelts.

children.label: → Scribes Carved Every Royal Deed
children.gloss: Queens stood proud on stelae; Needed 800 glyphs and calendars.

children.label: 2. Glyphs, Zero & Daily Cacao
children.gloss: Maya scribes painted bark-paper codices, invented place-value zero in base-20 maths, tracked Venus from El Caracol, traded cacao-bean cash, and played Pok-ta-Pok.

children.label: 3. Glyphs, Bark Books & Zero
children.q2Chain: 800 glyphs on stelae & fig-bark codices → Shell-dot-bar base-20 place-value zero → El Caracol Venus sightings link two calendars
children.gloss: 800 glyphs on stelae & fig-bark codices → Shell-dot-bar base-20 place-value zero → El Caracol Venus sightings link two calendars

children.label: 800 Glyphs & Fig-Bark Codices
children.gloss: Scribes mixed 800 word and syllable glyphs on Copán’s 63-step stairway and painted accordion-folded fig-bark books like the Dresden Codex.

children.label: 800 Word & Syllable Signs
children.gloss: Spelled any spoken Mayan sentence; 2,000+ glyphs on Copán stairway.

children.label: Fig-Bark Paper & Turkey Quills
children.gloss: Coated bark with white lime; Folded accordion Dresden Codex book.

children.label: → Needed Fast Base-20 Numbers
children.gloss: Carved royal dates on stelae; Counted huge sky cycles next.

children.label: Shell, Dot & Bar: Inventing Zero
children.gloss: Independently inventing place-value zero, Maya base-20 maths stacked numbers vertically using a shell (0), pebble dot (1), and bar (5).

children.label: Shell (0), Dot (1) & Bar (5)
children.gloss: Matched ten fingers, ten toes; Rome still lacked any zero.

children.label: Vertical Columns Tallied Sums Fast
children.gloss: Stacked ones, twenties, four hundreds; Counted market cacao, measured pyramids.

children.label: → Let Astronomers Map Bright Venus
children.gloss: Invented zero all on own; Calculated star paths across centuries.

children.label: El Caracol & Two Calendars
children.gloss: Sighting Venus through El Caracol’s round dome without glass telescopes, astronomers meshed the 260-day Tzolk’in and 365-day Haab’ calendars.

children.label: El Caracol Windows Tracked Venus
children.gloss: No glass telescopes needed indoors; Round tower at Chichén Itzá.

children.label: 260-Day Tzolk’in & 365-Day Haab’
children.gloss: Meshed together like two cogwheels; Clicked back every 52 years.

children.label: Guided Maize Planting & Feasts
children.gloss: Tzolk’in named lucky festival days; Solar Haab’ timed farm harvests.

children.label: 4. Maize, Cacao & Pok-ta-Pok
children.q2Chain: Limewater maize ground on stone metates → Cacao-bean cash, human porters & canoes → Hip-bouncing rubber balls in Pok-ta-Pok
children.gloss: Limewater maize ground on stone metates → Cacao-bean cash, human porters & canoes → Hip-bouncing rubber balls in Pok-ta-Pok

children.label: Limewater Maize & Frothy Cacao
children.gloss: Cooks soaked maize in limewater to unlock nutrients, ground tortilla dough on volcanic metates, and whipped chilli-spiced cacao.

children.label: Nixtamal Maize & Flat Tortillas
children.gloss: Limewater unlocked vital corn nutrients; Ground dough on stone metates.

children.label: Roasted Cacao Whipped With Chilli
children.gloss: Steamed tamales inside corn husks; Poured frothy honey-chilli royal drinks.

children.label: → Dried Cacao Beans Became Cash
children.gloss: Valuable seeds grew in pods; Used across shaded plaza markets.

children.label: Cacao Money, Porters & Canoes
children.gloss: Ten cacao beans bought a rabbit and a hundred bought a turkey, carried along stone causeways by forehead-strap porters and canoes.

children.label: 10 Beans Rabbit; 100 Turkey
children.gloss: Cheats stuffed clay inside shells; Market judges checked beans closely.

children.label: Forehead-Strap Porters & Canoes
children.gloss: Zero horses, oxen, wheeled carts; Paddled salt, obsidian, green jade.

children.label: → Crowds Gathered by Ballcourts
children.gloss: Walked white raised stone causeways; Filled plazas on festival days.

children.label: Sacred Pok-ta-Pok Ballcourts
children.gloss: Wearing thick leather-and-wood hip yokes, athletes dived to bounce a heavy 4kg solid rubber ball through stone rings without hands or feet.

children.label: 4kg Rubber Ball & Macaw Heads
children.gloss: Sloping limestone walls beside pyramids; Heavy bouncing ball bruised ribs.

children.label: Hip Yokes Only — No Hands
children.gloss: Hands and feet broke rules; Aimed high through stone rings.

children.label: Honoured Sun, Rain & Myth Twins
children.gloss: More than sport: sacred ritual; Echoed Hero Twins in Xibalba.

children.label: 3. Beliefs, AD 900 & Today
children.gloss: From Popol Vuh maize myths and Chichén Itzá’s 365-step serpent pyramid to the southern AD 900 drought shift and over seven million living Maya today.

children.label: 5. Maize Gods & Chichén Itzá
children.q2Chain: Popol Vuh maize humans & Chaac rain caves → El Castillo’s 365 solar steps → Equinox sunlit serpent Kukulkan glides down
children.gloss: Popol Vuh maize humans & Chaac rain caves → El Castillo’s 365 solar steps → Equinox sunlit serpent Kukulkan glides down

children.label: Popol Vuh, Xibalba & Chaac
children.gloss: The Popol Vuh told how gods kneaded humans from maize dough, while priests burned copal in cenote caves for rain god Chaac.

children.label: Mud & Wood Failed; Maize Worked
children.gloss: Mud crumbled; wood forgot thanks; Kneaded yellow, white maize humans.

children.label: Hero Twins & Chaac Rain Caves
children.gloss: Twins beat Xibalba lords playing; Burned copal resin for Chaac.

children.label: → Inspired Sky-Aligned Pyramids
children.gloss: Cenotes seen as underworld doors; Linked farming rains to stars.

children.label: El Castillo’s 365 Stone Steps
children.gloss: At Chichén Itzá, builders gave Kukulkan’s El Castillo four 91-step staircases plus one top platform to equal all 365 solar days.

children.label: Four 91-Step Stairs Plus Top
children.gloss: Dedicated to feathered serpent Kukulkan; 91 times 4 plus 1.

children.label: Priests Announced Planting Dates
children.gloss: Watched bright stars from summit; Called across wide northern plaza.

children.label: → Cast Moving Equinox Snake Shadow
children.gloss: Angled nine stone terraces precisely; Turned sunlight into living calendar.

children.label: Equinox Serpent Shadow Glides
children.gloss: Every spring and autumn equinox, seven sunlit triangles rippled down El Castillo’s northern stairs to join Kukulkan’s stone head.

children.label: Seven Sunlit Triangles Slithered
children.gloss: Equal day and night hours; Joined carved open-jawed snake head.

children.label: Unfading Indigo-Clay Maya Blue
children.gloss: Heated indigo leaves with clay; Celebrated rains and maize harvests.

children.label: Blended Maths, Astronomy & Faith
children.gloss: Northern Chichén Itzá boomed long; Thrived even as south shifted.

children.label: 6. AD 900 Shift & Living Maya
children.q2Chain: Drought, deforestation & war empty southern Tikal (c. 900) → Northern cenote cities & coastal Tulum boom → 7+ million Maya thrive today
children.gloss: Drought, deforestation & war empty southern Tikal (c. 900) → Northern cenote cities & coastal Tulum boom → 7+ million Maya thrive today

children.label: Three Linked Southern Causes
children.gloss: Southern cities like Tikal, Palenque, and Copán emptied around AD 900 due to three linked causes: drought, deforestation, and warfare.

children.label: Severe Multi-Year Drought Struck
children.gloss: Lake-bed snail shells prove drought; Dried stone southern reservoirs empty.

children.label: Deforestation & Royal Warfare
children.gloss: Lime plaster fires stripped hillsides; Soil washed; wars blocked trade.

children.label: → Families Moved North to Cenotes
children.gloss: Packed metates and walked north; Maya people never vanished away.

children.label: Northern Cenotes & Port Tulum
children.gloss: For centuries after AD 900, Postclassic northern cities near deep cenotes like Chichén Itzá and cliffside Caribbean Tulum boomed.

children.label: Chichén Itzá & Uxmal Boomed
children.gloss: Deep Yucatán cenotes held water; Thrived from AD 950–1520.

children.label: Cliffside Tulum Welcomed Sea Canoes
children.gloss: Walled port beside salt flats; Traded honey, cotton, bright feathers.

children.label: → Resisted Conquest Until 1697
children.gloss: Spanish friars burned bark codices; Four ancient books still survived.

children.label: Over 7 Million Maya Today!
children.gloss: Shattering the “vanished Maya” myth, over seven million Maya people speak 30+ languages, weave huipil cloth, and read glyphs today.

children.label: 30+ Languages & Huipil Looms
children.gloss: Over seven million proud Maya; Weave bright huipil on looms.

children.label: Modern Maya Read Ancient Glyphs
children.gloss: Live across Mexico, Central America; Farm golden maize; read stelae.

children.label: Shattered the “Vanished Maya” Myth
children.gloss: Endured 1500s diseases and steel; Living culture thrives proudly today.
